texts: Age over 1 year is not a criterion for the Fontan procedure: A.
What matters is the physiology: low pulmonary vascular resistance and pressure, unobstructed pulmonary venous drainage and adequately sized pulmonary arteries.
Good ventricular function and no more than mild or moderate atrioventricular valve regurgitation are needed too.
The Fontan is usually completed at 2 to 4 years of age, after a Glenn, but age itself is not one of the criteria.
In the picture, the four ticks are on the fountain's checklist and the age card is left off.
Memory hook: the fountain checks the pipes and the pump, not the birthday.
